source_text: –Ἐβουλόμην σε μικρὸν ἀναπνεῦσαι τῶν ἔργων τῆς ἀδικίας, καὶ δοῦναι σχολὴν τοῖς σεαυτοῦ λογισμοῖς, ὥστε ἐνθυμηθῆναι πρὸς ποῖον πέρας ἡ σπουδὴ τῶν γινομένων συντέταται. Ἔχεις γῆς ἀροσίμης πλέθρα τόσα καὶ τόσα, γῆς πεφυτευμένης τοσαῦτα ἕτερα, ὄρη, πεδία, νάπας, ποταμοὺς, λιβάδας. Τί οὖν μετὰ ταῦτα; Οὐχὶ τρεῖς σε πήχεις ἀναμένουσιν οἱ πάντες; Οὐχὶ λίθων ὀλίγων βάρος ἀρκέσει πρὸς φυλακὴν τῇ δυστήνῳ σαρκί; Ὑπὲρ τίνος μοχθεῖς; ὑπὲρ τίνος παρανομεῖς; Τί συνάγεις χερσὶν ἀκαρπίαν; Εἴθε ἀκαρπίαν καὶ μὴ ὕλην τῷ αἰωνίῳ πυρί. Οὐ νήψεις ποτὲ ἀπὸ τῆς μέθης ταύτης; Οὐχ ὑγιανεῖς τοὺς λογισμούς; Οὐ σεαυτοῦ γενήσῃ; Οὐ πρὸ ὀφθαλμῶν λήψῃ τὸ τοῦ Χριστοῦ δικαστήριον; Τί ἀπολογήσῃ, ἐπειδάν σε κύκλῳ περιστάντες οἱ ἠδικημένοι καταβοῶσί σου ἐπὶ τοῦ δικαίου κριτοῦ; Τί οὖν ποιήσεις; ποίους συνηγόρους μισθώσῃ; ποίους μάρτυρας παραστήσῃ; πῶς παραπείσεις τὸν ἀπαραλόγιστον δικαστήν; Οὐκ ἔνι ῥήτωρ ἐκεῖ· οὐκ ἔνι πιθανότης ῥημάτων, κλέψαι δυναμένη τοῦ δικαστοῦ τὴν ἀλήθειαν· οὐκ ἀκολουθοῦσιν οἱ κόλακες, οὐ τὰ χρήματα, οὐχ ὁ ὄγκος τοῦ ἀξιώματος· ἔρημος φίλων, ἔρημος βοηθῶν, ἀσυνηγόρητος, ἀναπολόγητος, κατῃσχυμμένος παραληφθήσῃ, σκυθρωπὸς, κατηφὴς, μεμονωμένος, ἀπαῤῥησίαστος. Ὅπου γὰρ ἂν περιαγάγῃς τὸν ὀφθαλμὸν, ἐναργεῖς ὄψει τῶν κακῶν τὰς εἰκόνας· ἔνθεν τοῦ ὀρφανοῦ τὰ δάκρυα, ἐκεῖθεν τῆς χήρας τὸν στεναγμὸν, ἑτέρωθεν τοὺς κατακονδυλισθέντας ὑπό σου πένητας· τοὺς οἰκέτας, οὓς κατέξαινες· τοὺς γείτονας, οὓς παρώργιζες· πάντα σοι ἐπαναστήσεται· πονηρὸς χορὸς τῶν κακῶν σου πράξεων περιστοιχίσεταί σε. Ὥσπερ γὰρ ἡ σκιὰ τῷ σώματι, οὕτω ταῖς ψυχαῖς αἱ ἁμαρτίαι παρέπονται, ἐναργῶς τὰς πράξεις ἐξεικονίζουσαι. Διὰ τοῦτο οὐκ ἔστιν ἄρνησις ἐκεῖ, ἀλλ' ἐμφράσσεται στόμα καὶ τὸ ἀναίσχυντον. Αὐτὰ γὰρ ἑκάστου καταμαρτυρεῖ τὰ πράγ ματα, οὐ φωνὴν ἀφιέντα, ἀλλὰ τοιαῦτα φαινόμενα οἷα ὑφ' ἡμῶν κατεσ κεύασται. Πῶς σοι δυνηθῶ ὑπ' ὄψιν ἀγαγεῖν τὰ φρικτά; Ἐὰν ἄρα ἀκούσῃς, ἐὰν ἄρα ἐνδῷς, μνήσθητι τῆς ἡμέρας ἐκείνης ἐν ᾗ· Ἀποκαλύπτεται ὀργὴ ἀπ' οὐρανοῦ· Μνήσθητι τῆς ἐνδόξου τοῦ Χριστοῦ παρουσίας, ὅτε ἀναστήσονται· Οἱ μὲν τὰ ἀγαθὰ πράξαντες εἰς ἀνάστασιν ζωῆς, οἱ δὲ τὰ φαῦλα εἰς ἀνάστασιν κρίσεως· Τότε αἰσχύνη αἰώνιος τοῖς ἁμαρτωλοῖς· Καὶ πυρὸς ζῆλος ἐσθίειν μέλλων τοὺς ὑπεναντίους· Ἐκεῖνα λυπείτω σε, καὶ μὴ λυπείτω ἡ ἐντολή. Πῶς σε δυσωπήσω; τί φθέγξομαι; Βασιλείας οὐκ ἐπιθυμεῖς; γέενναν οὐ φοβῇ; πόθεν εὑρεθῇ ἴασις τῇ ψυχῇ σου; Εἰ γὰρ τὰ φρικτὰ οὐ πτοεῖ, τὰ φαιδρὰ οὐ προτρέπεται, λιθίνῃ καρδίᾳ διαλεγόμεθα.
thought_title: The final judgment exposes the rich man's injustice
orientation: Basil is directly addressing the rich hearer, calling him to pause from his unjust labors and imagine the day of Christ's judgment, when his victims will surround him and his deeds will testify against him.
pass_a_gloss: I wanted you to breathe a little from the works of injustice, and to give leisure to your own reasonings, so as to consider toward what end the zeal of the things being done is stretched. You have so many and so many plethra of arable land, so many other plethra of planted land, mountains, plains, wooded valleys, rivers, meadows. What then after these things? Do not three cubits await you, all of them? Will not a weight of a few stones suffice for guarding the wretched flesh? For what do you toil? For what do you transgress the law? Why do you gather with your hands unfruitfulness? If only unfruitfulness and not fuel for the eternal fire. Will you not ever sober up from this drunkenness? Will you not make your reasonings healthy? Will you not become your own? Will you not take before your eyes the judgment seat of Christ? What will you say in defense, when the wronged, standing around you in a circle, cry out against you before the just judge? What then will you do? What advocates will you hire? What witnesses will you present? How will you persuade the undeceived judge? There is no orator there; there is no persuasiveness of words, able to steal the truth from the judge; the flatterers do not follow, not the money, not the bulk of dignity; bereft of friends, bereft of helpers, without advocate, without defense, put to shame you will be taken away, gloomy, downcast, isolated, without freedom of speech. For wherever you turn your eye around, you will see clear images of the evils; on one side the tears of the orphan, on the other the groaning of the widow, from another side the poor beaten by you; the household slaves whom you flayed; the neighbors whom you provoked to anger; everything will rise up against you; a wicked chorus of your evil deeds will stand around you. For just as the shadow follows the body, so sins follow the souls, clearly imaging the deeds. Because of this there is no denial there, but the mouth is stopped, even the shameless one. For the very things of each person testify against him, not uttering a voice, but appearing such as they were prepared by us. How could I bring the dreadful things before your sight? If then you listen, if then you yield, remember that day on which: Wrath is revealed from heaven; Remember the glorious coming of Christ, when they will rise: Those who did good things to a resurrection of life, but those who did evil things to a resurrection of judgment; Then eternal shame to sinners; And the zeal of fire about to eat the adversaries; Let those things grieve you, and let not the commandment grieve you. How shall I move you to shame? What shall I utter? Do you not desire the kingdom? Do you not fear hell? From where will healing be found for your soul? For if the dreadful things do not terrify, the bright things do not urge on, we are speaking to a stony heart.

lemmas.gloss: to breathe again, take a breather

choices.why: Keeps the agricultural metaphor of gathering a harvest that yields nothing, matching Basil's contrast with the fruitful use of wealth for the poor.
ὕλη here means combustible material; 'fuel' captures the sense that hoarded wealth feeds the fire of judgment.
The adjective means 'not to be deceived by false reasoning'; 'undeceived' preserves the judicial context and the impossibility of tricking Christ.
rejected: the judge who cannot be deceived

choices.why: ὄγκος means weight, mass, or pomp; 'bulk' conveys the heavy, imposing social status that will count for nothing at the judgment.
χορός evokes a tragic or theatrical chorus; 'chorus' keeps the image of the deeds surrounding and accusing the sinner as a collective.

choices.english: we are speaking to a stony heart
choices.why: The dative of the person addressed; 'stony heart' echoes biblical language of hardness of heart and keeps the direct address.
rejected: we are conversing with a heart of stone

bible_refs.note: οἱ μὲν τὰ ἀγαθὰ πράξαντες εἰς ἀνάστασιν ζωῆς, οἱ δὲ τὰ φαῦλα εἰς ἀνάστασιν κρίσεως
πυρὸς ζῆλος ἐσθίειν μέλλων τοὺς ὑπεναντίους

pass_b_english: I wish you would take a brief breather from your works of injustice and give your own thoughts some leisure, so that you might consider toward what end the pursuit of all these things is stretched. You have so many plethra of arable land, so many more of planted land, mountains, plains, wooded valleys, rivers, meadows. What comes after all this? Do not three cubits await you, like all the rest? Will not the weight of a few stones be enough to guard your wretched flesh? For whom do you labor? For whom do you act lawlessly? Why do you gather unfruitfulness with your hands? If only it were unfruitfulness and not fuel for the eternal fire. Will you never sober up from this drunkenness? Will you not make your thoughts healthy? Will you not come to yourself? Will you not set the judgment seat of Christ before your eyes? What will you say in your defense when those you have wronged stand around you in a circle and cry out against you before the righteous judge? What will you do then? What advocates will you hire? What witnesses will you produce? How will you persuade the judge who cannot be reasoned with? There is no orator there; there is no persuasiveness of words able to steal the truth from the judge. No flatterers follow you, no wealth, no bulk of dignity. Bereft of friends, bereft of helpers, without an advocate, without a defense, covered in shame you will be taken away—gloomy, downcast, alone, without boldness. For wherever you turn your eye, you will see vivid images of your evils: here the tears of the orphan, there the groaning of the widow, elsewhere the poor you beat with your fists, the servants you wore out, the neighbors you provoked to anger. Everything will rise up against you. A wicked chorus of your evil deeds will surround you. For just as a shadow follows the body, so sins follow souls, vividly imaging the deeds. Therefore there is no denial there, but the mouth is stopped, and shamelessness with it. For each person's own deeds testify against him, uttering no voice but appearing exactly as they were prepared by us. How can I bring the dreadful things before your eyes? If you will listen, if you will yield, remember that day on which wrath is revealed from heaven. Remember the glorious coming of Christ, when those who have done good will rise to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgment (John 5:29). Then there will be eternal shame for sinners, and the zeal of fire about to devour the adversaries (Isaiah 26:11 LXX). Let those things grieve you, and do not let the commandment grieve you. How shall I move you to shame? What shall I say? Do you not desire the kingdom? Do you not fear hell? From where will healing be found for your soul? For if the dreadful things do not terrify you, and the bright things do not urge you on, we are speaking to a stony heart.
notes: The source has πράγ ματα and κατεσ κεύασται with spaces mid-word, likely line-break artifacts in the manuscript or edition; glossed as πράγματα and κατεσκεύασται.

problems.why: οἱ πάντες here means 'everyone' (all people), not 'the whole of you' — the point is all people get three cubits.
problems.fix: Do not three cubits await you, like everyone else?
problems.ruling: οἱ πάντες = 'all people/everyone,' not 'the whole of you'; universal claim about all humans, not this individual.

problems.source_quote: Καὶ πυρὸς ζῆλος ἐσθίειν μέλλων τοὺς ὑπεναντίους
problems.why: The Greek quotes Isaiah 26:11 LXX, not Hebrews 10:27.
problems.ruling: Source 'πυρὸς ζῆλος ἐσθίειν μέλλων τοὺς ὑπεναντίους' matches Isaiah 26:11 LXX, not Hebrews 10:27.

fixed: Changed 'the whole of you' to 'like everyone else' because 'οἱ πάντες' means 'everyone' (all people), not 'the whole of you'.
Changed 'Hebrews 10:27' to 'Isaiah 26:11' because the Greek 'Καὶ πυρὸς ζῆλος ἐσθίειν μέλλων τοὺς ὑπεναντίους' quotes Isaiah 26:11 LXX, not Hebrews 10:27.

problems.why: οἱ πάντες here means 'all [three cubits],' i.e., the same three cubits await all; not 'like everyone else.'
problems.fix: Do not three cubits await you, like all the rest?
problems.ruling: οἱ πάντες = 'all [people],' not 'all [three cubits]'; 'like everyone else' misreads syntax.

problems.why: ἀπαράλογιστος means 'who cannot be reasoned with / persuaded by argument,' not 'undeceived.'
problems.fix: the judge who cannot be persuaded
problems.ruling: ἀπαράλογιστος = 'not to be reasoned with,' not 'undeceived'; meaning changed.

problems.why: τὸ ἀναίσχυντον is nominative/accusative neuter, not 'mouth'; it means 'shamelessness' or 'the shameless person.'
problems.fix: but the mouth is stopped, and shamelessness with it
problems.ruling: τὸ ἀναίσχυντον = 'the shameless one/thing,' not 'mouth'; no noun supplied, misleading.

problems.quote: the wrath of God is revealed from heaven (Romans 1:18)
problems.why: Source says 'wrath from heaven,' not 'wrath of God'; the LXX Psalm 78 (MT 79) has 'wrath of God,' but Basil's quote omits 'of God.'
problems.ruling: Source omits θεοῦ; translator added 'of God' without brackets, misrepresenting quotation.

problems.ruling: πυρὸς ζῆλος ἐσθίειν μέλλων τοὺς ὑπεναντίους matches Nahum 1:10 LXX, not Isaiah 26:11.

τὸ ἀναίσχυντον is neuter, meaning 'shamelessness' or 'the shameless thing'; 'and shamelessness with it' preserves the sense.

problems.why: κατέξαινω means 'wore out, exhausted with toil,' not 'flayed' (which would be ἐξέδειρα).
ἀπαρρησίαστος means 'without boldness/confidence,' not 'freedom of speech' (παρρησία as boldness before God/judge).

refereed.source_quote: Καὶ πυρὸς ζῆλος ἐσθίειν μέλλων τοὺς ὑπεναντίους
refereed.why: The Greek quoted does not match Isaiah 26:11 LXX, which reads differently; this appears to be a misidentification. The phrase 'πυρὸς ζῆλος' with 'ἐσθίειν μέλλων' is closer to other texts or a free formulation.
refereed.fix: Remove the '(Isaiah 26:11 LXX)' citation or verify correct source.
refereed.ruling: Source phrase 'πυρὸς ζῆλος ἐσθίειν μέλλων τοὺς ὑπεναντίους' does not match Isaiah 26:11 LXX wording; misidentification misleads reader.
